description: GASP Standard ontology: entities, source categories, fields, and their relationships to metrics. Platform-agnostic: defines the canonical structure businesses map their warehouse to.

entities.label: Customer
entities.definition: A distinct billing entity with one or more subscriptions. The "who" of your business relationship.

entities.label: Subscription
entities.definition: A billable agreement between a customer and your product, with defined terms, pricing, and status. The "what and when" of the relationship.

entities.label: License
entities.definition: A specific capability, quantity, or configuration granted by a subscription. The "how much" of the relationship.

entities.label: Lead
entities.definition: A person or company that has shown interest but has not been qualified as a sales opportunity.

entities.label: Opportunity
entities.definition: A qualified sales prospect with an estimated value, stage, and expected close date.

entities.label: User
entities.definition: An individual who uses the product. In B2B, one Customer may have many Users. Usage metrics are measured at this level.

entities.label: Ticket
entities.definition: A discrete support interaction initiated by a customer or user, tracked to resolution.

entities.label: Employee
entities.definition: An internal team member. People metrics and efficiency ratios (revenue per employee) are measured at this level.

entities.label: Invoice
entities.definition: A billing document representing money owed or collected. Cash flow and collections metrics are measured at this level.

entities.label: Partner
entities.definition: An external organization that sources, influences, or resells deals. Partner metrics are measured at this level.

entities.label: Project
entities.definition: A professional services engagement with defined scope, timeline, and deliverables.

entities.label: Plan
entities.definition: A pricing tier offered to customers (e.g. Starter, Pro, Enterprise). Each plan defines a price point and a set of included products and quotas.

entities.label: Product
entities.definition: A distinct purchasable unit within the company's offering (e.g. Analytics Module, Automation Module). A subscription may include multiple products.

entities.label: Campaign
entities.definition: A marketing initiative with defined objectives, channels, budget and dates. Campaigns source leads and influence opportunities.

entities.label: Contact
entities.definition: A named individual at a customer account involved in the buying or expansion process. Distinct from User (product user) and Lead (pre-qualification).

concepts.label: Revenue (GAAP)
concepts.definition: Recognized revenue under accrual accounting. The financial outcome of delivering on subscription obligations.

concepts.label: Bookings
concepts.definition: The total value of new contracts signed in a period. A forward-looking commitment that converts to revenue over the contract term.

concepts.label: COGS
concepts.definition: Cost of Goods Sold: the direct cost of delivering the product, infrastructure only (hosting, compute, payment processing, delivery software). Support, success engineering, implementation and onboarding are subtracted in Gross Margin's Operating form, not in COGS. Subtracted from revenue in Gross Margin.

concepts.label: Cohort
concepts.definition: A time-bound grouping of customers by acquisition period. Used for retention and expansion analysis to isolate vintage effects.

concepts.label: Pipeline
concepts.definition: The aggregate weighted value of active opportunities. Represents potential future bookings at various probability stages.

concepts.label: Segment
concepts.definition: A classification of customers by size, vertical or fit (e.g. SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise). Used for cohort analysis and benchmark comparison.

concepts.label: TCV (Total Contract Value)
concepts.definition: The total value of a contract over its full term, including one-time fees and multi-year commitments. Distinct from Bookings (period-attributable) and ACV (annualized).
concepts.provenance: definitions.md: Bookings vs ACV vs TCV

accessControl.description: Recommended sensitivity and access scope per metric. These are GUIDANCE, not enforcement. Actual policies should be expressed in Cedar, OPA, or warehouse RLS. See /v1/governance for the framework.

sensitivityTiers.public: Shareable externally with no restriction (rare for internal SaaS metrics)
sensitivityTiers.internal: Shareable across the organization. Default for most operational metrics
sensitivityTiers.confidential: Cross-functional but sensitive. Typically restricted to managers and above
sensitivityTiers.restricted: Highly sensitive. Executive and finance-leadership only by default

accessScopes.unscoped: Same value for everyone with access (e.g. company-wide ARR)
accessScopes.department-scoped: Filtered by the viewer's department context
accessScopes.owner-scoped: Visible only for records the viewer owns or manages (individual, team, territory, book or segment: interpretation lives in the adapter)

structuredFormulas.description: Derived from formulas.json by `npm run derive` (gasp-wiki-mcp). Each graph metric: its canonical formula, the metrics it reads (with arithmetic role and polarity: how the metric moves when the input rises) and the fields it reads, for graph traversal.

activation_rate.expression: count_distinct(field.customer_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date) and field.activation_date is not null) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where in_period(field.onboarding_completion_date))

arpa.expression: metric.mrr / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_end

at_risk_rate.expression: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.composite_score < 40) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.composite_score is not null)

cac.expression: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')

cpl.expression: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm' and field.cost_centre = 'marketing') / metric.leads

csat.expression: count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.satisfaction_score >= 4) / count(field.satisfaction_score where field.survey_type = 'customer')

employee_turnover.expression: count_distinct(field.employee_id where field.termination_date >= period_start and field.termination_date <= period_end) / ((metric.total_headcount at period_start + metric.total_headcount at period_end) / 2)

enps.expression: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'employee') * 100

feature_adoption.expression: count_distinct(field.user_id where field.feature_id is not null) / count_distinct(field.user_id where field.product_event_type = 'qualifying')

grr.expression: (metric.mrr at period_start - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)
grr.adjustedVariant: (sum(field.mrr_start) + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type in ('contraction', 'churn') and field.change_nature = 'permanent')) / sum(field.mrr_start) over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

logo_churn_rate.expression: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'churn') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.customer_status = 'active') at period_start

magic_number.expression: (metric.arr - lag(metric.arr, 1 quarter)) / lag(window(sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm'), 1 quarter), 1 quarter)

marketing_cac.expression: sum(field.cost where field.cost_function = 'gtm' and field.cost_centre = 'marketing') / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.event_type = 'new')

marketing_sourced_pipeline.expression: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.marketing_source = 'marketing' and field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'))

nps.expression: (count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.nps_score >= 9) - count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer' and field.nps_score <= 6)) / count(field.nps_score where field.survey_type = 'customer') * 100

nrr.expression: (metric.mrr at period_start + metric.expansion_mrr - metric.contraction_mrr - metric.churned_mrr) / metric.mrr at period_start over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)
nrr.adjustedVariant: (sum(field.mrr_start) + sum(field.mrr_change where field.event_type in ('expansion', 'contraction', 'churn') and field.change_nature = 'permanent')) / sum(field.mrr_start) over cohort(field.customer_id, period_start)

partner_sourced_revenue.expression: sum(field.opportunity_amount where field.partner_sourced = true and field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

pipeline_value.expression: sum(field.opportunity_amount * field.stage_probability where field.opportunity_stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost'))

pqas.expression: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.criteria_met = true) at period_end

qbr_completion.expression: count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.qbr_completed = true) / count_distinct(field.customer_id where field.qbr_due = true)

renewal_rate.expression: count_distinct(field.subscription_id where field.renewed = true and in_period(field.contract_end)) / count_distinct(field.subscription_id where in_period(field.contract_end))

sales_cycle.expression: median(field.close_date - field.opportunity_created_date where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date))

win_rate.expression: count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage = 'closed_won' and in_period(field.close_date)) / count(field.opportunity_id where field.opportunity_stage in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') and in_period(field.close_date))

entityRelationships.description: Entity-to-entity and entity-to-concept edges that model the SaaS business structure. These complement the metric-to-entity MEASURES edges to form a complete digital twin.

edges.description: A customer holds one or more subscriptions. Hierarchy Principle 1: customers own subscriptions, not the reverse.
A subscription grants one or more licenses (seats, entitlements, feature access). Hierarchy Principle 3: licenses are derived from subscriptions.
In B2B SaaS, one customer organization has many product users. Usage and engagement metrics are measured at the user level.
Customers open support tickets. Support volume and resolution metrics are measured at the ticket level.
A qualified lead converts into a sales opportunity. This is the MQL→SQL transition in the acquisition funnel.
A won opportunity creates a new customer (closed-won). This is the SQL→Customer transition.
A channel partner sources or influences deal opportunities. Partner-sourced vs. direct pipeline is a key attribution metric.
CSMs and account managers are assigned to customer accounts. Employee efficiency and coverage ratios are measured through this relationship.
edges.provenance: Salesforce OwnerId pattern, CS Platform assignment

edges.description: Professional services projects are delivered to customers. Project margins and utilization are measured through this relationship.
Subscriptions generate recognized revenue over their term as obligations are fulfilled.
Subscriptions generate periodic invoices according to their billing schedule.
Closed-won opportunities produce bookings. Bookings convert to revenue over the contract term.
edges.provenance: CRM reporting: Opportunity Amount at close

edges.description: Active opportunities contribute to pipeline value, weighted by stage probability.
Delivering on subscriptions incurs costs (hosting, support, onboarding) that form the COGS basis for Gross Margin.
edges.provenance: REA duality: give-event paired with take-event

edges.description: Each customer belongs to an acquisition cohort based on their start date. Cohort analysis isolates vintage effects in retention and expansion.
Self-referential edge for account hierarchy. Global enterprises with subsidiaries roll up to a parent customer. Used for global account ARR and consolidated reporting.
edges.provenance: Salesforce Parent Account, Zuora Account hierarchy

edges.description: A subscription is priced according to a plan. Many subscriptions can share the same plan. Enables tier-mix analysis, upgrade-path metrics and packaging health.
edges.provenance: Stripe Subscription→Price, Zuora Rate Plan, Chargebee Plan

edges.description: A license grants access to one or more products (modules). A subscription can include multiple products, each governed by its own license entitlement.
edges.provenance: Auth0 entitlements, Stripe Entitlements API, custom IAM

edges.description: A customer account is represented by named individuals (champions, decision makers, executive sponsors). Enables buying-center coverage metrics and stakeholder mapping.
A marketing campaign sources leads. Captures attribution beyond the free-text source field. Enables campaign ROI, channel-mix, and sourced-pipeline metrics.
Each customer belongs to a segment classification (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) based on size, ARR or fit. Segment is the foundational lens for cohort and benchmark comparisons.
Closed-won opportunities produce TCV (Total Contract Value). Distinct from Bookings (period-attributable) and ACV (annualized): TCV captures the full multi-year commitment value.
edges.provenance: Salesforce Opportunity Amount across full term, CFO reporting
